data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["The CPU relies on active convective cooling to maintain steady state, while the city relies on passive radiative cooling.","Heat generation in a CPU is purely electrical; in a city it includes metabolic, combustion, and solar-origin components.","The CPU heat is continuous, while a large fraction of urban anthropogenic heat has diurnal variation."],"overturn_conditions":["If natural surface-atmosphere energy fluxes swamp anthropogenic inputs in the nocturnal balance.","If population density is found to be a poor proxy for anthropogenic heat flux across diverse cities."],"shared_structure":["Persistent internal heat generation maintaining elevated temperature.","Temperature gap proportional to the rate of internal heat generation."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_004"],"transfer_claims":["Just as a CPU under load stays warmer than its surroundings due to internal heat generation, a city stays warmer due to anthropogenic heat.","Just as reducing CPU load lowers the temperature gap, reducing population density or energy use lowers the UHI."]},"claim":"The nocturnal UHI is sustained by anthropogenic heat emissions from vehicles, industry, and buildings.
